rationale: This observational spatial-ecological study analyzes 1,881 groundwater-supplied drinking water service areas in Arizona over 10- and 20-year periods using geostatistics, clustering, and multivariate regressions. Its central rule-based exposures belong to institutional_structure_coordination: statutory groundwater management boundaries under the 1980 Groundwater Management Act (Active Management Areas vs. Non-Designated Areas) and jurisdictional primacy allocation under the Safe Drinking Water Act (Tribal vs. State oversight). It also compares regulated community water systems against unregulated private domestic well areas (regulatory_model_ownership) and examines SDWA Maximum Contaminant Level compliance/monitoring differences (enforcement_sanctions), though jurisdictional governance and management boundaries clearly dominate. The focal empirical outcomes are groundwater quantity/depletion trends (availability/functional sustainability) and drinking water potability/contamination risk (arsenic and nitrate concentrations, detections, and MCL exceedances), all falling squarely within effective_access.
